identification.summary: TA459 is Proofpoint's name for a threat actor it believes operates out of China and that typically targets Central Asian countries, Russia, Belarus, Mongolia and others [S1][S2]. Proofpoint documented it using PlugX, NetTraveler and ZeroT through spear-phishing [S1][S3][S4].
identification.firstObserved: Proofpoint first-reported campaign began in July 2015 (possibly earlier) against telecom and military targets in Russia [S2]. A search summary of third-party reporting says activity dates to at least 2013, which this research did not verify against a primary source [S6].
identification.notes: Vendor name TA459 (Proofpoint); MITRE group G0062 [S5]. No Microsoft name mapping is recorded in the actor record. Some copies of Proofpoint text contain the typo 'TA549' for TA459 [S1]. NetTraveler malware is also tracked by Kaspersky under other actor naming; not merged here.

attribution.confidence: Proofpoint says it believes the actor operates out of China [S1][S2]. In the NetTraveler coverage, Proofpoint's Patrick Wheeler said the group was Chinese but there was 'no indication that it is state-sponsored' [S7].
attribution.basis: Proofpoint campaign analysis of lures, infrastructure and malware reuse across 2015-2017 [S1][S2][S3]. No government attribution was found in the sources gathered.

objectives: Espionage-style collection against telecom, military, defense and weapons-manufacturing targets in Russia and neighbours, pro-democracy and human-rights groups, and financial analysts covering telecoms [S2][S3][S4]. Specific end-user intent is not stated by sources beyond targeting patterns.

targeting.notes: Sectors and regions from Proofpoint reporting and press coverage of it [S1][S2][S3][S4]. Financial analysts in 2015 were described as collateral to telecom targeting and in 2017 as a primary lure theme [S1][S2].

capabilities.summary: Spear-phishing with RAR self-extracting archives on lookalike domains imitating Russian military and defense sites, delivering PlugX in 2015 [S2]. In 2016, links to RAR-packed executables and Word attachments exploiting CVE-2012-0158 delivered NetTraveler [S3][S4]. In 2017, Word documents exploiting CVE-2017-0199 dropped ZeroT, which downloaded PlugX [S1]. Other malware attributed in secondary coverage: Saker, Netbot, DarkStRat and a Gh0st RAT variant [S6]. MITRE lists PlugX, gh0st RAT, NetTraveler and ZeroT for the group [S5].

campaigns.name: PlugX against Russian telecom and military
campaigns.summary: Proofpoint observed a campaign beginning July 2015 (possibly earlier) and continuing into August, using PlugX in RAR self-extracting archives on fake domains impersonating Russian military and defense sites; Russian-speaking financial analysts covering telecoms were also hit [S2].

campaigns.name: NetTraveler against Russia and neighbours
campaigns.summary: Proofpoint reported a switch from PlugX to NetTraveler with otherwise similar TTPs; lures were RAR-packed executables and Word documents exploiting CVE-2012-0158, aimed at weapons makers, military, and pro-democracy and human-rights groups in Russia, Mongolia, Belarus and other European countries [S3][S4].

campaigns.name: Financial analysts and CVE-2017-0199
campaigns.summary: Spear-phishing Word attachments exploiting CVE-2017-0199 delivered ZeroT, which downloaded PlugX, against financial analysts covering the telecom sector; Proofpoint linked it to the 2015 activity [S1][S6].

diamond.adversary: China-based actor tracked by Proofpoint as TA459; state sponsorship not asserted by Proofpoint [S1][S7].
diamond.capability: Spear-phishing, Office exploits (CVE-2012-0158, CVE-2017-0199), PlugX, NetTraveler, ZeroT [S1][S3][S5].
diamond.infrastructure: Lookalike domains imitating Russian military and defense sites hosting RAR self-extracting archives [S2]; further C2 details not gathered.
diamond.victim: Russian telecom and military, regional defense and weapons makers, human-rights and pro-democracy groups, telecom financial analysts [S2][S3][S4].
diamond.technology: Email, unpatched Microsoft Office on user endpoints [S1][S3].

gaps: Proofpoint pages could not be fetched (DNS failure in this environment); content relies on search-result summaries of Proofpoint, Security Affairs, SC Media and Infosecurity Magazine, so details should be verified against the primary posts.
Exact publication dates for the 2015 PlugX post and the 2016 NetTraveler post were not confirmed; year-level dates are used. The 2017 post is described in search output as April 2017.
No activity after 2017 was found; current status is unknown.
No government attribution or sponsor identified; Proofpoint's quoted remark (SC Media) is that there is no indication of state sponsorship [S7].
No Microsoft actor name mapping verified.
Claims of activity since 2013 and the 'Saker, Netbot, DarkStRat' list come from secondary summaries and are unverified [S6].
